I'm ready to play Monopoly.

Reviewing the completed trade details. I gave ST_CHARLES_PLACE to p2 and received $40 plus INDIANA_AVENUE.

The trade event contradicts the counter offer. I now own ST_CHARLES_PLACE and STATES_AVENUE, with $1046 cash.

p2 owns Indiana and Kentucky. p3 owns Tennessee and Illinois. p4 owns New York. I now hold States and St. Charles as the two pink properties.

Virginia is still unowned, so building is impossible. p3 holds Illinois and blocks the red set. Trading cannot acquire an unowned property.

Oranges are split between p3 and p4, with St. James unowned. All other color sets are unowned. I have no cash pressure, so mortgaging is unnecessary. Trading cannot acquire the unowned Virginia.

I cannot trade for Virginia because it is unowned. p3's Tennessee and Illinois do not complete any set I need. p2 wants Illinois from p3, but that would not help me. Light blues are all unowned, so no trade is needed there.

Future-option trades are impossible under the current rules. No cheap incomplete set is available to complete immediately. p2 now holds two reds and will likely pursue Illinois from p3.

A red monopoly would be devastating. I considered buying Illinois from p3 to block p2, but that would waste cash on a property that cannot help me build. The classic strategy is to prioritize completing my own set.

Blocking p2's red set would require paying cash or a utility for Illinois. That would give p2 a red monopoly. I should not trade with p3 to block p2.

I am now weighing whether to buy Illinois from p3 to block p2's red monopoly. It would cost roughly $300, leaving about $746 after Virginia and house construction. p3 may refuse to sell it since they know it completes the red set.

I now think buying Illinois from p3 would be too expensive. They might demand $300 to $400 for a property that cannot help me build. Trading with p4 is also useless because I cannot complete the orange set. I will end my turn.

I will conserve cash for Virginia, light blues, yellows, greens, and Park Place. I am also considering a speculative trade with p3 to prevent p2 from completing the red set.

I will not publicly signal my desire for Virginia. Downplaying its importance might make others skip it, but since I already own two pinks, the unowned Virginia is obvious and likely to be bought at a premium or auctioned. Telegraphing desperation would only invite higher bids.
